title: Standardization of Input-Output Coefficient Declarations
summary: The NBR evolved a standardized reporting framework for manufacturers to declare input-output coefficients for finished products. This moved from general procedural requirements to specific, industry-tailored templates that mandate the disclosure of waste percentages and raw material consumption per unit of finished product.

evolution.structure: Transitioned from general regulatory compliance to highly specific, product-category-based reporting templates.
evolution.scope: Expanded from basic industrial goods to complex electronic and mechanical finished products.

timeline.change: Introduction of standardized industry-specific declaration templates for pre-fabricated buildings and motorcycles.
Expansion of the standardized declaration template to include electronics like air conditioners, ATMs, and CCTV cameras.
Further expansion of the standardized declaration template to include lift manufacturing.

The declaration requires detailed information including the item names, H.S. Codes, unit specifications, and specific quantities of materials used both with and without waste percentage calculations.
